summary: F. B. J. Kuiper worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at Leiden University (~1925–1934), he succeeded Jean Philippe Vogel in 1939 and held a post at Leiden University from 1939 to 1972.

Fa Qing is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a dissertation at the University of Calgary under doctoral supervisor Leslie S. Kawamura and interim supervisor A. W. Barber, alongside other teachers. He later taught Nirupam Chakma and Yong Hua Shi.

Fabienne Jagou is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. She completed her PhD at the École des hautes études en sciences sociales (~1994–1999) and became a Maître de conférences at the École française d'Extrême-Orient around 2001.

Fabio Rambelli works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Mentored by Allan G. Grapard and William F. Powell, he held posts at Sapporo University as Associate Professor (2001–2002) and Professor of Religion and Semiotics (~2000–2010).

Fabrizia Baldissera specializes in Indology. She studied at the Department of Mathematics "Federigo Enriques" (1969–2004) and held posts at the University of Florence (~2000) and the University of Naples "L'Orientale".
Fafang was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taixu. He held an appointment as a Research Fellow in Indian Buddhism at Visva-Bharati University.

Fang-kuei Li worked in linguistics, Sinology, and Tibetology, studying at Tsinghua University (~1921–1924) and the University of Michigan (~1924–1926). He held posts at Chicago (~1927–1929), Yale (~1937–1939), Washington (~1949–1969), and Hawaii (~1969–1973).
Fausto Gherardo Fumi specialized in linguistics and Indology. He studied under Giuseppe Bardelli at the Scuola Normale Superiore's Classe di Lettere e Filosofia from around 1858 to 1862.

Fazun was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Drepung Monastery and under Taixu. He founded the Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute, served as translator for the National Ethnic Affairs Commission (1950), and led the Buddhist Academy of China.

Ferdinand Benary worked in linguistics and religious studies. He studied under Franz Bopp (~1827–1829) and was appointed an associate professor in the theological faculty at Humboldt University of Berlin in 1831.

Ferdinand Diederich Lessing worked in Sinology, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He taught at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1925–1935) and the University of California, Berkeley (~1935–1952), teaching Helmut Hoffmann and Alex Wayman.

Ferdinand Justi was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. After studying at the University of Marburg (~1854–1856) and under Theodor Benfey (~1856–1859), he held a post at Marburg from around 1865 to 1907.

Ferdinand Sommer was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Freiburg (~1894–1898). He held posts at Basel, Leipzig, Rostock, Jena, Bonn, and finally as a professor at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1926–1951).

Ferdinand de Saussure was a linguist and Indologist who studied in Geneva, Leipzig (under Curtius and Brugmann), and Berlin (under Oldenberg and Zimmer). He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1880–1891) and the University of Geneva (1891–1913).
Fernando Jose Benetti is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Nalanda University under doctoral supervisor Aleksandra Wenta.

Fernando Tola worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies after studying at the National University of San Marcos (~1932–1943). He held posts at the University of Buenos Aires (~1964–1984) and served as director of the Instituto de Investigaciones Budistas (~1989–2017).

Filippo Marsili is a scholar in Sinology and history and archaeology. He pursued graduate studies at the University of California, Berkeley, where his teachers included Patricia Berger, and later held a post at Saint Louis University.

Finnian M. M. Gerety specializes in Indology and religious studies. After earning a doctorate from Harvard University by 2015, he held a postdoctoral fellowship at Yale (2017–2018) and a visiting assistant professorship at Brown University (attested 2020).

Fitzedward Hall was an Indologist who studied at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (~1840–1842) and Harvard University (~1842–1846). He later held a post at King's College London from around 1862 to 1869.

Flavio A. Geisshuesler is a Tibetology and religious studies scholar educated at Lausanne, Bern, and Virginia (PhD ~2014–2019 under David Germano). He was a postdoctoral researcher at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (2019) mentored by Dan Martin (~2020–2022).
